section_title: What does carrying one another’s burdens look like?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 2 Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

context_lines: This verse belongs to [Galatians 6:1–5](https://thewayofscripture.com/passages/galatians-6-1-5.html), where Paul tells believers to restore someone caught in sin with gentleness and to watch their own vulnerability to temptation.
Carrying another person’s burdens gives practical shape to the love described in 5:13–14. It helps explain what fulfilling the law of Christ looks like in shared life.

The surrounding warning against pride matters. The helper must examine his own work, and each person remains responsible for his own conduct. Paul brings mutual help and personal responsibility into the same paragraph.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand the law of Christ here as the call to love expressed through practical help. [Wesley’s note on verse 2](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-galatians/) describes sympathy and assistance in weaknesses and trials, and the [USCCB note on verse 2](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/galatians/6) connects it with serving one another through love.
god_plan_lines: [John 13:34–35](https://biblehub.com/bsb/john/13.htm) connects love among Jesus’ disciples with His own love for them. [1 John 3:16–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_john/3.htm) makes the connection concrete: Jesus laid down His life for us, and love for others is to take shape in action, including help for a brother in need.

These passages show how mutual burden-sharing belongs to God’s larger work through His Son. The love shown in Christ’s self-giving becomes visible in a family that cares for its members. Helping one another is part of making that love known.
current_position_lines: Our study [What Is the True Church?](https://thewayofscripture.com/studies/true-church.html), in its section on bearing one another’s burdens, understands this as costly, practical care within God’s family. Sharing a burden means walking with someone through the struggle, offering sustained presence and help. The study treats that shared life as love in action, made possible by grace.

editorial_review.position_source_detail: What Is the True Church? — We Bear One Another’s Burdens; content/studies/true_church.md:131–141, direct6:2 quotation. Limited to practical mutual care, without importing unchecked claims about entire denominations.
